chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from a number of our companions from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from a number of our companions from Ibn Bukayr from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The divorce of the boy is valid if he has reached the age of discernment, and so is his will and his gift, even if he has not had his first seminal emission. The divorce of the sick person is not valid; if he divorces, they inherit each other as long as she is in the waiting period. If her waiting period ends, she inherits him, and he does not inherit her, for a period between them and one year, provided she has not married. If she marries, she has no inheritance. If it exceeds the year by one day, she has no inheritance. There is no difference in all these rulings whether the divorce is the first, the second, or the third, or if it is a divorce of the Sunnah or a divorce of the waiting period, for the ruling is the same in all of them. What indicates this is what he narrated:
ai.seo_question: What are the rules of divorce and inheritance for a sick person and a young boy in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: From al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith clarifies that a boy’s divorce is valid upon reaching *‘aql* (discernment) even without *ihtilam* (seminal emission), while a sick person’s divorce is suspended until recovery. It further establishes that inheritance rights between the couple persist during the *‘iddah* and for one year thereafter, provided the wife has not remarried, a rule consistent across all types of divorce. This reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on the continuity of marital bonds and financial rights during the transitional period of separation.
